solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Pub turned over at first by the French mob

indicators.note: turned over means the pub word is flipped to read backwards

parts.note: a bar is a pub

indicators.note: at first means only the opening letter of by is used

parts.note: le is French for the

explanation.surface: A pub crowd has been overturned early on by a French mob.
explanation.definitionFit: A disorderly crowd, a mob, is a synonym; both mean an unruly throng of people.

clue.text: Managed shop primarily, accepting order for book

indicators.note: accepting means the managed and shop letters take the order inside

parts.note: ran means managed, as in ran a business
OM is the Order of Merit

indicators.note: primarily means take the first letter of shop

explanation.surface: Someone ran a shop and accepted an order for a book.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Paul's epistle to the church in Rome is a book of the New Testament.

clue.text: Seek a hob for cooking outside university food establishment

indicators.note: outside means the mixed letters go round the university letter
cooking means the letters of seek a hob are mixed up

explanation.surface: Look for a stove for cooking outside a university canteen.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a place where bread is made is an establishment producing food.

clue.text: Harris's neighbour's wife, draped in garlands

indicators.note: draped in means the wife letter is wrapped in the garlands

parts.note: leis are Hawaiian flower garlands

explanation.surface: Harris's neighbour's wife is draped in flower garlands.
explanation.walkthrough: Harris looks like a person, but it is the southern part of the Outer Hebridean island of Lewis and Harris, Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Geography: the northern part of the same Hebridean island adjoins Harris.

clue.text: Acceptable area and time to digest European question

indicators.note: to digest means the time word swallows the European and question letters inside it

parts.note: a date is a point in time

explanation.surface: An acceptable deal: a European question gets time and space to be digested.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something good enough to pass muster is both acceptable and sufficient.

clue.text: Remove vote from female nurse once husband is in country

parts.note: Di is a woman's name, short for Diana
SEN was a State Enrolled Nurse, a former British nursing grade

indicators.note: in means the husband and is letters go inside the country

parts.note: France is a country

explanation.surface: Taking the vote from a woman who was once a nurse because her husband lives abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to strip someone of the right to vote is to deprive them of the franchise.

clue.text: Who in Paris initially buys glitzy jewellery, finding fault?

parts.note: qui is French for who

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of buys

parts.note: bling is showy jewellery

explanation.surface: A question about who in Paris buys flashy jewels, while criticising.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: raising petty objections is nitpicking, carping over trifles.

clue.text: Question a graduate, initially having a port

indicators.note: initially having means the second a in the clue is placed at the start

parts.note: BA is a Bachelor of Arts, a graduate

explanation.surface: Interviewing a graduate who first had a port.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Jordan's only seaport, on the Red Sea, is a port town.

clue.text: Interrupting English match, aim to correct errors

indicators.note: interrupting means the aim word breaks into the other letters

parts.note: to mate is to match or pair
an end is an aim or goal

explanation.surface: Breaking into an English game with the aim of fixing mistakes.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to emend a text is to correct its mistakes; this is a rarer variant.

clue.text: How some purchases are made — the opposite with deliveries

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six deliveries
counter means opposite, contrary

explanation.surface: Some purchases are made the opposite way, with home deliveries.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: medicines sold directly across the shop counter without prescription are bought this way.

clue.text: Some stylists may do it to stir things up

definitions.meaning: hairdressers can put ripples into hair, a literal reading of the phrase
the idiom for causing a disturbance or upsetting the status quo

explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: creating a fuss or trouble is the figurative sense, while setting ripples in hair is the literal one.

clue.text: Article in trendy magazine ultimately lacking sense

indicators.note: in means the article sits within the other letters

parts.note: in means fashionable, trendy

indicators.note: ultimately means take the final letter of magazine

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A piece in a fashion magazine turns out, in the end, to be pointless.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something silly and without sense is foolish or vacuous.

clue.text: Form of 24 a Mitford aristocrat backed?

indicators.note: backed means the aristocrat's title is read backwards

parts.note: the Mitford sisters, daughters of a peer, were Honourables, and Nancy Mitford wrote of their childhood society of Hons

explanation.surface: A question whether a type of theatre might be a Mitford aristocrat in reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 24 is DRAMA. The Hon. is the courtesy title for a peer's child; the Mitfords were a famous English aristocratic family of sisters.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the classical masked theatre of Japan is one kind of stage play.

clue.text: Way extremely sharp gang stole first diving aid

indicators.note: first means everything before it comes ahead of the way word
extremely means take the extreme letters, first and last, of sharp

parts.note: a ring is a gang of criminals
a boa is a stole, a long scarf of feathers or fur
RD is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: A sharp gang stole something first, then got away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stole' looks like a verb of theft but is the scarf. 'first' puts SP, RING and BOA ahead of RD.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a flexible board for jumping off into a pool is a piece of diving equipment.

clue.text: Pig-headed Greek character taking his novel on lake

indicators.note: on means the following letters are placed after the lake letter

parts.note: mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: novel means new, so the word his is rearranged

explanation.surface: A Greek person writes a novel about a lake, stubbornly.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: obstinate like a mule, which is the animal behind the word, means stubborn.

clue.text: Close relative's crazy about conforming to established usage

indicators.note: about means the crazy word goes round the relative

parts.note: idiotic means crazy
ma is mother, a close relative

explanation.surface: A close relative is crazy about following the rules.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: natural to native speakers, following the accepted way of saying things.

clue.text: Clothing torn to pieces when keeping goal

indicators.note: keeping means the torn word holds the goal word inside it

parts.note: rent is a past tense of rend, to tear apart
an aim is a goal

explanation.surface: Clothes ripped apart while saving a goal, like a goalkeeper's shirt.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: raiment is an old literary word for garments or attire.

clue.text: Leader takes time going over college, so to speak

indicators.note: going over means the time word is turned backwards

parts.note: tide is an old word for time, as in Eastertide

indicators.note: so to speak means the college's name as spoken

parts.note: Oriel is a college of Oxford University

explanation.surface: A leader takes time to go over a college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader' suggests a chief, but here it is a newspaper's opinion column.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: in British newspapers, the main opinion article is called a leader.

clue.text: French author's point about old Italian painter

indicators.note: about means the author and point letters surround the old letter

parts.note: Jules Verne was a French novelist
SE, south-east, is a compass point

explanation.surface: A French author makes a point about an old Italian painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Paolo Veronese was a Venetian Renaissance painter.

clue.text: Sad European stage where you'll find rabble

parts.note: a leg is a stage of a journey or race
rabble is the answer to 1 across in this grid, written 1ac, which reads as the letters I A C

explanation.surface: A gloomy European stage full of riff-raff.
explanation.walkthrough: The rabble is the answer at 1 across: 1 ac, read as letters, gives IAC.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: mournful, lamenting poetry, an elegy, makes the adjective mean sorrowful.

clue.text: Mug about to return goods conforming to latest fashion

indicators.note: to return means the about word is read backwards

parts.note: on means about, concerning
G is the abbreviation for good, so goods doubles it
in means fashionable

explanation.surface: A mug for returning fashionable goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mug' looks like a cup or a fool, but here it is slang for the head.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang: both words are informal terms for a person's head or face.

clue.text: Fashionable environment for introduction of liveried servant?

indicators.note: environment for means the fashionable word surrounds the letter

parts.note: funky means fashionable, cool

indicators.note: introduction of means the first letter of liveried

explanation.surface: A trendy setting to introduce a servant in livery.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a liveried manservant or footman, often used of a lackey.

clue.text: Surprised-looking writer encountering "trap" in dictionary

indicators.note: in means the writer and trap words go inside the dictionary

parts.note: OED is the Oxford English Dictionary
a pen is a writing instrument
trap is slang for the mouth, as in shut your trap

explanation.surface: A writer looks surprised to find a 'trap' in the dictionary.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a gaping jaw is the classic look of astonishment.

clue.text: Head of exceptionally light African antelope

indicators.note: head of means take the first letter of exceptionally

parts.note: to light is to land, as a bird lights on a branch

explanation.surface: The head of an exceptionally light antelope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'light' looks like an adjective about weight, but it is the verb to alight.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the largest antelope of the African savanna.

clue.text: Sensation in music academy described by American lawyer

indicators.note: described by means the lawyer goes round the academy, drawing a line about it

parts.note: DA is a District Attorney, an American prosecutor
RAM is the Royal Academy of Music

explanation.surface: A scene at a music academy, as reported by an American lawyer.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: excitement or a stir caused by events, as in a lot of fuss and commotion.

clue.text: See about eating with a wise-looking person

indicators.note: eating means the reversed see word takes the with letter inside it
about means the see word is turned round

parts.note: lo is an old word for look, see

explanation.surface: Watch someone looking wise while eating.
explanation.definitionFit: Figurative sense: a solemn person is likened to the bird traditionally seen as wise.

clue.text: Perform in French before a court

indicators.note: before means the French word comes ahead of the rest

parts.note: en is French for in

explanation.surface: Acting in French in front of a court.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to carry out or act out a role is to perform it.

clue.text: Antipodean army's obsession with north

parts.note: the TA is the Territorial Army, the British volunteer reserve, so army's gives TA's
a mania is an obsession

explanation.surface: An Antipodean army is obsessed with the north.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: someone from the island state south of mainland Australia comes from the Antipodes.

clue.text: Finish fish, chewing over part of fruit

parts.note: an end is a finish
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over
a carp is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: Finish the fish while chewing over a bit of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chewing over' suggests mulling something; 'over' gives O and 'chewing' only glues the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: botanically, the hard inner layer round a seed, like a cherry stone, is a part of the fruit.

clue.text: Grain from a mountainous island, some say

indicators.note: some say means the island's name as spoken, in a non-rhotic accent, matches a cereal

parts.note: Bali is a mountainous Indonesian island

explanation.surface: Grain from a hilly island, as some would have it.
explanation.walkthrough: In southern British speech, with the R silent, the island and the grain sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a cereal crop used for malting and animal feed is a grain.
